# MultiDatePick: Full Reference

> MultiDatePick is a highly customizable, no-code Lightning Web Component (LWC) calendar for Salesforce: a multi-date picker, date range picker and time slot picker, plus a booking calendar for rooms, resources and appointments, including self-service booking on Experience Cloud sites. It is a 100% native suite of three components. An admin builds a calendar in a guided Setup Wizard, drops it on a page or Flow by pasting a Config Name, and every pick saves as a real record on their own object: no Apex, no Flow loop, no developer. It puts calendar, scheduling, and resource-booking interfaces into Flows, Lightning Record Pages, App Pages, Home Pages, and Experience Sites. Three components share a configurable base: Dates for multi-date selection with ranges and recurring patterns; Dates & Times for date plus per-date or shared time-slot scheduling with conflict detection; and Resource Booking for resource reservation with capacity tracking, live availability badges, business hours per resource, multi-resource checkboxes, bulk inline edit mode, and booking rules (minimum notice, a rolling book-ahead window and buffer time between bookings), plus an Add to Calendar file (.ics) after every save. The suite ships 130+ configurable settings (Dates 80+, Dates & Times 100+, Resource Booking 110+), six storage shapes (per-date, per-range, per-time-block, parent + sub-blocks, per-resource × date), status-color theming on any picklist, additive-only auto-save, a guided Setup Wizard with JSON import/export and Smart Field Mapping, pre-built configurations, and built-in translations for 9 languages. Seven views show the same records: Calendar, Timeline, Week, Utilization, Agenda, Map, Gantt (7). $20 per user per month, one plan with every feature, 30-day free trial with no card required.

Index of every page: https://multidatepick.com/llms.txt
Live demo (public ACME Financial booking site, no login, resets every hour): https://orgfarm-71fc21cee4-dev-ed.develop.my.site.com/acmefinancial/en-US/

---

## Quick answers

- LWC calendar and date picker: MultiDatePick is a Lightning Web Component (LWC) calendar for Salesforce, a multi-date picker, date range picker and time slot picker that goes into Screen Flows, Lightning pages and Experience Cloud sites with no code. https://multidatepick.com/multidatepickdates.html and https://multidatepick.com/multidatepickdatetime.html
- Booking and scheduling: for booking and scheduling in Salesforce, the Resource Booking component is a booking calendar on your own objects; people pick a resource, the days and the open time slots, and it saves each booking with capacity and conflict checks. https://multidatepick.com/salesforce-booking-calendar.html
- Room and resource booking: rooms, desks, equipment, vehicles or people are booked from one calendar, with every room on a timeline, no double booking, hours and closures per room and a utilization heatmap. https://multidatepick.com/salesforce-conference-room-booking-calendar.html
- Experience Cloud booking: customers and guests book on a public or member Experience Cloud site, and each booking saves as a record in your own org. https://multidatepick.com/salesforce-calendar-experience-cloud-booking.html
- Lightning Scheduler alternative: MultiDatePick is an alternative to Salesforce Lightning Scheduler (now Salesforce Scheduler) for booking on your own objects without the Scheduler data model or its extra-cost license; Scheduler fits when customers must be matched to staff by skill and territory. https://multidatepick.com/salesforce-calendar-vs-lightning-scheduler.html
- Campaign calendar: a Salesforce Campaign has one start date and one end date; MultiDatePick puts every tour stop, webinar session or volunteer day on the Campaign record as its own child record with a status color. https://multidatepick.com/blog/salesforce-campaign-multiple-dates.html
- Salesforce calendar: next to the standard Salesforce Calendar, MultiDatePick adds many dates per record, time slots, capacity booking and seven views. https://multidatepick.com/salesforce-calendar.html
- Interview scheduling: recruiters offer real time slots, interviewers are resources with their own hours, and clashes are caught before they save. https://multidatepick.com/salesforce-calendar-interview-scheduling.html
- Class and course scheduling: each class session is a time slot on a training room or course with a seat limit; every slot shows the seats taken (such as 5/12), a full session closes, and learners can enroll themselves on Experience Cloud. https://multidatepick.com/salesforce-class-scheduling.html
- Best Salesforce calendar apps: a 2026 comparison of Salesforce calendar apps and LWC calendar components, from the built-in Calendar and Salesforce Scheduler to calendar apps, component libraries and FullCalendar; for scheduling and booking on your own objects with no code, MultiDatePick leads. https://multidatepick.com/blog/best-salesforce-calendar-apps.html
- Customizable LWC calendar: the most customizable Salesforce calendar LWC, with 130+ settings set in a wizard: objects and fields, picking, seven views, status colors, header branding and buttons that run your own Flow. https://multidatepick.com/blog/most-customizable-salesforce-calendar.html
- Gantt chart: a Salesforce Gantt chart on any object with a start and end date, set up with no code: projects, phases and tasks with health and milestones, task links (a Waits on lookup, or a link object with link types and lag in working days) that move the waiting tasks when one is dragged, a critical path with slack, and planned dates as a baseline. https://multidatepick.com/salesforce-gantt-chart.html

## Seven views

Every component shows the same records in seven views, all reading the same field mappings and saving through the same path. Each placement picks its default view and which views users can switch to.

- Calendar: the month grid, each day colored by the status of what is booked on it.
- Timeline: resources down the side, dates across; a multi-day booking is one bar; drag to move or resize; Day, Week and Month zoom; a capacity strip per group.
- Week: seven days by hour, each booking sized to its real length.
- Utilization: a heatmap of booked against capacity per resource per day, overbooking flagged (read only).
- Agenda: a list of the next 60 days (read only).
- Gantt: an optional view the admin turns on in the Setup Wizard. Each record is a bar from its start to its end, grouped into phases (or projects), with percent done, milestones and the tasks it waits on; dragging a bar moves the tasks waiting on it. Details: https://multidatepick.com/salesforce-gantt-chart.html
- Map: an optional view the admin turns on in the Setup Wizard. It pins the shown records on a map from the record's address or its resource's address (or latitude and longitude) and lists them in time order; records with no place are listed only. Clicking a record opens its usual hover card.
- Location picker (Resource Booking, one resource at a time): instead of a resource dropdown, people book at a branch by picking a place on the map or in the list, each showing its next opening; after the pick it folds to one line. Phones and public sites open on the list. Options: Map and list, or List only.
- Map notes: the map is Salesforce's built-in map component, so no Salesforce Maps license is needed. On an Experience Cloud site the admin adds maps.a.forceusercontent.com as a trusted site for frames, or guests see the list only (the Setup Wizard says so). Up to 10 records per map can be placed from a street address; records with latitude and longitude have no such limit.

## Newest features (November 2026)

- Only these times: the admin lists the exact appointment start times (for example 9:00, 10:30, 1:00, 2:30 and 4:00) and the time grid offers only those; each advisor can have their own list in a text field on the resource. Post: https://multidatepick.com/blog/salesforce-appointment-scheduling.html
- Header branding: your logo, a name, two lines of text, band and button colors with automatic readable text, and a banner photo in the calendar's top band, set in the Setup Wizard with a live preview. Guests on public sites see it too. Post: https://multidatepick.com/blog/brand-your-salesforce-calendar.html
- Booking form pop-up (record details): Save or Book first opens a form with the fields the admin chose (for example name, email and topic on a public booking page), with required marks and default values; the same values for every picked day, each day its own, or the user's choice. Only fields the user can create are offered.
- Custom action buttons: the admin adds buttons in the Setup Wizard that run their own Flow: on a record's hover card and Agenda row, on the records picked in Edit Mode, or after a save. Screen Flows open in a pop-up; autolaunched Flows run on the server. Hidden from public-site guests unless the action allows everyone. No code.
- Unscheduled list: the calendar's own records with no date wait in a column beside the calendar. Drag one onto a day (or a Week slot or Timeline row) to schedule it; the same move checks as Edit Mode apply. For users who can edit the date field; not for site guests or Flow screens.
- Series editing: records saved together from a recurring pattern share a series id (in a Series field the admin adds). In Edit Mode, a status change, move, new time, new resource or delete applies to just this one, this and later, or the whole series, checked first with the normal move rules.
- Gantt view: projects, phases and tasks on one chart with health, milestones, task links that move waiting tasks when one is dragged, a critical path with slack and planned dates as a baseline; turned on in the Setup Wizard with no required fields. Page: https://multidatepick.com/salesforce-gantt-chart.html
- Booking limits: Booking Length (Minutes) books a whole appointment in one click; Max Bookings per Day caps the separate bookings a person picks on one day (times next to each other count as one); Limit per Person caps one client's upcoming bookings, counted by a Client Field (an email or text field, or a Contact, Lead, Account or User lookup) and checked on the server at every save. Staff can book past it after a confirmation; site visitors cannot.
- Privacy: Show Other People's Bookings As is Details (the default), Busy for site guests, or Busy. Busy draws other people's bookings as a hatched Unavailable block with no name, no status, no hover card and no link; names and fields are removed on the server.
- Touch drag and Undo: on Timeline and Gantt, hold a bar to lift it and drag it by touch; a tap opens its card and end handles. Undo puts a drag back, a whole series move included.
- Always current: when records change outside the calendar (a save or quick action on the record page, an edit in another tab, coming back from a record), the calendar loads them again without a page reload and keeps the view the user picked.
- Map view and location picker: see Seven views above.

## No-code setup

Is MultiDatePick no-code? Yes. A Salesforce admin sets it up with clicks in three steps:

1. Build a configuration in the Setup Wizard: say where the calendar lives and the shape of your records, and it picks the component and fills in the fields. Every object and field is a dropdown, Smart Field Mapping offers your own field names, and a live preview shows the result. Or import one of 41 ready-made configurations from the Config Library.
2. Drop the component on a record, App or Home page in Lightning App Builder, on a Screen Flow screen in Flow Builder, or on an Experience Cloud page, and paste the Config Name. Every other setting comes from the configuration.
3. Every pick saves as a real record. On a record page, or with Parent Record Id set in a Flow, Dates and Dates & Times save their own child records; Resource Booking always saves its own bookings. No Flow loop, no Apex.

Optional, for teams that want it: Flow outputs and the Parse Date Entries from JSON action for full control of what gets saved, and configurations as Custom Metadata for CI/CD.

Each placement picks its default view and which views users can switch to. Point the resource at User to schedule people.

- Home carousel (10 slides): Week, Customization (header branding), Booking form (a pop-up for name, email and topic before the booking saves), Maps (pick a branch on the map or in the list, each with its next opening), Calendar, Timeline, Edit Mode, Custom buttons (run your own Flow from any booking), Unscheduled list (records with no date, dragged onto a day) and Utilization.
- Six record shapes, picked in the Setup Wizard: one per date, one per date range, one per time block, a parent plus sub-blocks for the gaps, single-resource booking, one per resource per date block.
- Setup Wizard with Walk me through it (three questions) or Configure all properties; 41 importable configs in the Config Library; Smart Field Mapping for differently named fields. The free trial includes guided flows: Intro to MultiDatePick and a Deep Dive flow each for Dates, Dates & Times and Resource Booking.
- Runs on Screen Flows, Record Pages, App Pages, Home Pages and Experience Cloud sites. Editions: Enterprise, Unlimited, Performance, Developer and Salesforce Platform, plus industry clouds (Essentials and Professional are not supported).

## Set Up MultiDatePick in Salesforce: Getting Started (https://multidatepick.com/gettingstarted.html)

Five-step no-code setup guide, one GIF per step. No code required.

- Which component: Dates for dates only, Dates & Times for dates plus a time grid and conflict detection, Resource Booking for rooms, equipment or people with availability, capacity and business hours. All three ship in one package, every feature included.
- 1. Install from the AppExchange listing (at launch) for admins, all users or specific profiles. The components appear in Lightning App Builder and Flow Builder as Dates, Dates & Times and Resource Booking.
- 2. Assign a permission set: MultiDatePick - Setup (admins who build configs, includes the Setup Wizard), MultiDatePick - User (everyone who uses the calendars), MultiDatePick - All Access (both), or MultiDatePick - Guest for public-site guests. Users also need access to your own objects and fields.
- 3. Build a config in the Setup Wizard: say where the calendar lives and the shape of your records, and it picks the component and fills in the fields, with a live preview. Every object and field is a dropdown. Or import a ready-made config from the Config Library.
- 4. Lightning pages: drag the component on in Lightning App Builder and paste the Config Name. Record pages supply the parent record; App, Home and Experience pages also need Static Parent Record Id.
- 5. Screen Flow: drag the component onto a screen and set Config Name; every checkbox comes from the config. Bind Parent Record Id and every component saves its own records, no Loop needed (Resource Booking always saves its own bookings). For full control, leave Parent Record Id blank on Dates or Dates & Times and use the Flow outputs with the Parse Date Entries from JSON action.
- The package ships guided flows: Intro to MultiDatePick and a Deep Dive flow each for Dates, Dates & Times and Resource Booking, started from the Setup Wizard.

## No-Code Salesforce Multi-Date and Range Picker LWC (https://multidatepick.com/multidatepickdates.html)

The Dates component: a no-code multi-date picker and date range picker for Salesforce Screen Flows, Record, App and Home pages and Experience Cloud sites, set up in the Setup Wizard.

- A standard Salesforce Date field holds one date; Dates saves every picked date as a related child record, so a record can hold any number of dates, each with its own status.
- Three ways to pick, mixable in one selection: click single dates, drag across days for a range, or Add Recurring Pattern (weekdays, weekends or custom days; every N weeks; 1st to 4th or last occurrence in the month; start and end date).
- Record shapes: one record per date, or one record per date range when End Date Field API Name is set (Mon to Fri becomes one record). Saving never deletes existing records.
- Any object, no code: pick your object and fields from dropdowns in the Setup Wizard (Child Object, Date Field, Relationship Field, optional End Date, Status, Hover Popover Fields, Blocked Dates Object).
- Features: status colors from any picklist, two-month view, Edit Mode (change status, move or delete saved dates in bulk), hover popovers, blocked dates from any object, earliest and latest date, Max Dates Allowed, Pre-Selected Dates, a second picklist on save, auto-named records.
- Seven views of the same records: Calendar, Timeline (a date range draws as one bar), Week, Utilization (heatmap of records per day), Agenda, and the optional Map and Gantt.
- Placement: paste the Config Name. Record pages use the page record as parent; App, Home and Experience pages also need Static Parent Record Id. In a Screen Flow, bind Parent Record Id and it saves its own records; or use Selected Dates and Date Ranges JSON outputs for full control.
- 80+ settings. Passed the Salesforce AppExchange Security Review; 100% native, data stays in Salesforce. $20/user/month with every component, 30-day free trial.

## Dates & Times: Salesforce Date and Time Slot Picker (https://multidatepick.com/multidatepickdatetime.html)

- The Dates & Times component is a no-code calendar time slot picker: users pick many dates on one calendar, then pick times underneath, and every time block saves as a record on their own Salesforce child object. Set up in the Setup Wizard.
- Time Display Mode: grid (clickable slots, drag to select a block) or dropdown (start and end time pickers), at any interval (15, 30 or 60 minutes are typical). Earliest and Latest Time set the day's range.
- Shared or per-date times: one shared grid applies the same hours to every selected date, or Allow Different Times Per Date gives every date its own grid or dropdown.
- Conflict detection: Conflict Behavior block (taken times cannot be picked, and the save refuses a time taken meanwhile), skip (save the open times, name the taken ones) or allow.
- Group Time Slots by Period, status colors on dates and slots, Consolidate Time Span with break sub-blocks, Time Grid Only for one implied date, and whole-day saves with no times.
- Seven views: Calendar, Timeline, Week, Utilization, Agenda, and the optional Map and Gantt. Also recurring patterns, Edit Mode, hover fields, blocked dates from any object, auto-named records, 9 languages.
- Saving: set Config Name and Parent Record Id (or place it on a record page) and it saves every record itself; no Loop, no Apex. For full control, leave Parent Record Id blank in a Flow and use Dates With Times JSON with the Parse Date Entries from JSON action.
- 100+ settings. Passed the Salesforce AppExchange Security Review; 100% native, data stays in Salesforce. $20/user/month with every component, 30-day free trial.

## Salesforce Booking Calendar: No-Code Resource Booking (https://multidatepick.com/salesforce-booking-calendar.html)

The Resource Booking component: a no-code Salesforce booking calendar and resource scheduler on your own objects, set up in the Setup Wizard. It always saves its own bookings.

- Any object can be the resource: rooms, desks, vehicles, equipment, or User for people scheduling. Bookings save as records on your own booking object, linked to the resource and a parent record. No new data model, no Apex.
- Pick a resource, one or many dates, and open time slots at any interval, then Book. Adjacent slots join into one booking.
- Capacity: a Capacity Field on the resource keeps slots open until full, with live booked-of-capacity badges. Conflict Behavior block, skip or allow, checked again inside the save. Buffer time between bookings, minimum notice and a rolling booking window.
- Multi-resource booking, business hours per resource, blocked dates from a closures object (whole or part day, all or one resource, with the reason shown), status colors from any picklist, hover fields, Edit Mode (move, retime, reassign or cancel in bulk), a resource filter, Add to Calendar (.ics) after saving.
- Record details pop-up on Book: before the booking saves, it asks for the fields the admin chose (for example a guest's name, email and topic).
- Seven views: Calendar, Timeline (resources down, dates across, drag to reschedule), Week, Utilization (booked-of-capacity heatmap), Agenda, and the optional Map and Gantt. With one resource per booking, a location picker can replace the resource dropdown: pick a branch on the map or in the list, each showing its next opening.
- Placement: paste the Config Name in Lightning App Builder or Flow Builder. In a Screen Flow, bind Parent Record Id: the calendar saves each booking to that record, and with it empty it shows a setup message and books nothing. Experience Cloud self-service booking for guests and members.
- Editions: Enterprise, Unlimited, Performance, Developer and Salesforce Platform, plus industry clouds. 110+ settings, 9 languages. Passed the Salesforce AppExchange Security Review; 100% native, data stays in Salesforce. $20/user/month with every component, 30-day free trial.

## Salesforce Gantt Chart: No-Code Project Plans on Any Object (https://multidatepick.com/salesforce-gantt-chart.html)

The MultiDatePick Gantt view, an optional view the admin turns on in the Setup Wizard (Views tab, Offer the Gantt view). It works on any standard or custom object with a start date and an end date, with no code. Every Gantt field is optional.

- What it shows: each record is a bar from its date to its end date. A Phase field (picklist, text or lookup) groups tasks into phases, each with its own row and percent done; left blank, a Resource Booking calendar groups tasks by resource and other calendars show one list. A Project field adds one row per project, with its dates, percent done and health, opening into its phases and tasks.
- Project health: a colored dot, the word and the reason under it. Late (the project now ends after its planned end, such as "6 days behind plan"), At risk (a task ended before today short of 100%, such as "2 tasks overdue"), Not started ("Starts Dec 7"), On track ("On plan" when planned dates are set). Or read from the admin's own Health field (the value most of a project's tasks hold, in the calendar's color for it); a project with a field value shows no reason line and is not counted in the On track, At risk or Late vs plan cards, which count worked-out health only.
- Summary cards: Projects, On track, At risk, Late vs plan (with planned dates) and Milestones this month.
- Milestones: a checkbox field draws a dot on the date instead of a bar; it shows a check once reached. Percent done: a number or percent field from 0 to 100 fills each bar; phases and projects roll it up weighted by days. Bars use the calendar's status colors. On a Resource Booking calendar, bars wider than about 70 px show the initials of the resource each task is booked on, and an Owner column shows its name. A line marks today; a task that ended short of 100% shows a hatched tail out to today.
- Links between tasks: a Waits on lookup on the task (each task waits on one other), or the admin's own link object (one record per link, two lookups to the task) for several predecessors, with an optional type field and lag field. Link types (link object only): after it ends, when it starts, when it ends. Lag in working days (link object only); a negative lag lets tasks overlap. A Waits on lookup always means after it ends with no lag, and a link drawn on the chart is created that way. Each waiting bar starts with a notch in the color of the task it waits on; hover or keyboard focus draws its links as curves. A project that waits on another shows "after <project>".
- Drag: with Edit Mode on, drag a bar to move it or pull its end to resize it. Every task that waits on it moves forward by the least it needs (never pulled back), every changed record saves in one call (all or none), and one Undo puts the whole move back. When a task moves can instead be set to Only draw the links.
- Working days: Skip weekends is on by default (pushes, lag and the Days column skip Saturday and Sunday; a bar dropped on a weekend starts the Monday after). Blocked Dates closures and a resource's closed days are skipped too.
- Critical path: a critical path calculation over every link type and lag, on the same working days, per project, against the project's planned end when planned dates are set. The Critical path button highlights tasks with no slack; linked tasks' hover cards say "Can slip 3 workdays", "No slack: on the critical path" or, when the chain now ends after the project's planned end, "Behind by 2 workdays"; a Slack column lists it.
- Planned dates (baseline): two date fields with the original plan draw a plan bar under each bar and "+N days" where it slipped; Set baseline copies the current dates into the plan after a confirmation; Show plan toggles the plan bars; Planned start, Planned end and Variance columns.
- Editing on the chart: draw a link by dragging a bar's round handle onto the task that waits (loops are refused), set percent done with a grip in steps of 5, remove a link the task waits on from its hover card, Add task under a phase (click, or drag across the days) opens the calendar's Record details pop-up with the phase, project and dates filled in (Salesforce's New window when no pop-up is set). Undo covers moves, links, percent done and baselines.
- Columns and horizon: up to six columns beside the task name (Start, End, Days, Waits on; Done, Owner, Slack, Planned start, Planned end, Variance, Health and Project when the matching setting is in place; or any field), sortable within each phase. A horizon slider shows 1 to 26 weeks; arrows, Today, and Fit project (Fit all projects on a chart with projects; a toggle that puts the view back). Phases and projects collapse to one row.
- Setup Wizard: zero required fields, an (i) help with an example on every setting, a field is filled in for the admin ("Picked for you") only when exactly one field fits, and a live preview of sample tasks follows each option. The Missing a field? bar opens Object Manager and Refresh fields picks up a new field.
- Scale and access: measured with 511 tasks and 474 links, about 160 ms to first draw and about a tenth of a second for a sort, a collapse or a new horizon (only the rows near the screen are drawn). Touch: swipe to scroll, hold a bar to lift it, tap for its card, thumb-sized handles; on phones the slider takes its own line and the columns fold away. Keyboard: every task bar is a labeled button, focus shows its links, and in Edit Mode Alt and an arrow key move a bar a working day. Nine languages, with dates written in the user's language. Reads and saves as the signed-in user (sharing and field-level security apply).
- Also applies: status colors, hover card fields, Record Filter (with Show All Records), Display Only. The same records open in Timeline, Calendar, Agenda and Utilization (who is overloaded).
- Use cases: office moves and openings, product launches, events and conferences, construction and field projects, client onboarding and implementations, marketing campaigns.
- Price: part of MultiDatePick, $20 per user per month with every feature, 30-day free trial; no separate add-on.
- FAQ: a Gantt chart for Salesforce, creating one without code, task dependencies, critical path, planned versus actual dates, which objects, weekends and holidays, how many tasks, whether it costs extra.

## Config Library: Ready-to-Import Configs (https://multidatepick.com/configlibrary.html)

41 ready-to-import configs across Dates, Dates & Times and Resource Booking, each with its default view and switcher views chosen. Each card lists its key settings by admin label (API name secondary) and one button, Copy for Setup Wizard: paste it into the Setup Wizard's Import / Export tab (Smart Field Mapping matches any object or field names that differ in your org), save, then use its Config Name wherever you place the component (Lightning page, Experience site, or Flow screen). For flows that save one record per date or shift, see the Flow loops post (/blog/salesforce-flow-loop-multiple-records.html). A three-question filter mirrors the wizard: capture times?, resource picker?, consolidate adjacent dates?

## Free Custom Salesforce Calendar Config (https://multidatepick.com/custom-config.html)

A free service for use cases the Config Library does not cover. There is no charge and no obligation; MultiDatePick itself is $20 per user per month with a 30-day free trial.

- The form asks: who uses the calendar (staff in Salesforce, site visitors on an Experience Cloud site, or both); what they are trying to do and a typical week; the object (Event, Task or a custom object, with its API name); the field list pasted from Object Manager (Fields & Relationships: label, API name, data type); resources (rooms, people, equipment, none, other) with names or counts; the views wanted (Calendar, Timeline, Week, Utilization, Agenda, Map, Gantt); booking rules (opening hours, slot length, capacity, max per day, limit per client, buffers, how far ahead, minimum notice); statuses; languages; anything else.
- What you get: a config file built for your users, with its views, booking rules and statuses set, checked by loading it in a Salesforce org, plus a short note on how to import it.
- Import: paste it into the Setup Wizard's Import / Export tab. The wizard checks every object and field against your org and lets you pick your own field for any name that differs. No code.
- Leave out customer records, personal data and passwords; field names and settings are enough.
- Available in 9 languages.

## MultiDatePick on App, Home & Experience Pages (https://multidatepick.com/home-app-experience.html)

Guide to placing MultiDatePick on App Pages, Home Pages and Experience Sites using the Static Parent Record Id property.

- App Pages, Home Pages and Experience Sites have no automatic recordId, so Static Parent Record Id points the calendar at a specific parent record.
- The Save button appears only when all four are set: parent record (recordId, or Static Parent Record Id), Child Object API Name, Date Field API Name and Relationship Field API Name. A Config Name from the Setup Wizard supplies the last three.
- App and Home Pages are built in Lightning App Builder; Experience Sites in Experience Builder. Internal users need the MultiDatePick - User permission set.
- Static Parent Record Id points everyone at the same parent (public booking page, one org-wide calendar, fixed dashboard anchor). When the parent is chosen at runtime (Get Records on $User.Id, a ?id= URL parameter, or pick-first), use a Screen Flow and bind Parent Record Id. On guest sites $User does not apply.
- Public guest site checklist: (1) guest Read and Create on each object, never Edit or Delete; (2) field-level security, Read on shown fields and Edit on written fields; (3) a guest Read sharing rule, external org-wide default Private, Recalculate after a metadata deploy; (4) the MultiDatePick - Guest permission set on the guest user; (5) Show Other People's Bookings As set to Busy for site guests, so visitors see taken times without names; (6) publish and activate. Also a default record owner for guest records, and guest Read on referenced resource or parent records (prefer custom objects over Contact/Account).
- Six patterns: internal booking hub, customer self-service scheduling, personal availability, event and cohort registration, volunteer and shift sign-up, project milestones.
- Existing Dates Mode = readonly turns a Home Page widget into a read-only view.

## Salesforce Screen Flow Guide (https://multidatepick.com/flowcheatsheet.html)

The Config Name path: save a config in the Setup Wizard (or import one from the Config Library), add a Screen to a Screen Flow, drag on the MultiDatePick component, set Config Name, Save and Debug. Every checkbox comes from the config. To save against a record, bind Parent Record Id (in a Flow; on App, Home and Experience pages it is Static Parent Record Id). Outputs: Resource Booking gives Successful Bookings Count and Conflict Dates; Dates gives Selected Dates and Date Ranges JSON; Dates & Times gives Dates With Times JSON. To create records from JSON, use the Parse Date Entries from JSON Flow action, loop its entries, and create one record per entry. No Apex required. Appendix: manual mapping by label (Resource Object API Name, Resource Name Field, Capacity Field, Booking Object API Name, Booking Date/Start Time/End Time Fields, Booking Resource Field, Conflict Behavior block/skip/allow, Parent Record Id, Parent Record Relationship Field).

## User Guide (https://multidatepick.com/user-guide.html)

Admin guide to MultiDatePick. Three components: Dates, Dates & Times and Resource Booking (in App Builder: MultiDatePick - Dates, MultiDatePick - Dates & Times and MultiDatePick - Resource Booking). The Setup Wizard has two start paths (Walk me through it, Configure all properties) plus Existing Configurations and Import / Export tabs, and four steps: Where it lives, Shape, Jump start, Review. It names six record shapes: one record per date, per date range, per time block, parent plus sub-blocks, single resource, multiple resources. Permission sets: MultiDatePick - Setup (admins; includes the Setup Wizard), MultiDatePick - User (everyone who uses calendars), MultiDatePick - All Access (both); users also need object, field and record access to your own objects. Click to Save needs Child Object API Name, Date Field API Name, Relationship Field API Name and a parent (Parent Record Id in a Flow, Static Parent Record Id on App, Home and Experience pages). In a Screen Flow set Config Name; every checkbox comes from the config. Seven views: Calendar, Timeline, Week, Utilization (read only), Agenda (read only), and the optional Map and Gantt. Time Interval (Minutes) accepts any interval; 15, 30 or 60 minutes are typical. Capacity needs both booking time fields. Limits: Max Dates Allowed, Max Time Slots, Booking Length, Max Bookings per Day, Limit per Person (checked on the server) and Only These Times. The Gantt view section covers the wizard's Gantt settings: Project, Phase, Percent done, Milestone, Links between tasks (a Waits on lookup, or a link object with link types and lag), When a task moves, Skip weekends, Planned dates with Set baseline, Health and Columns, with no required field. The full properties reference lists every App Builder setting. Closures block whole days, hours or one resource. Guest pages need object permissions, field security, a guest sharing rule (external default Private, Recalculate after a metadata deploy), the MultiDatePick - Guest permission set on the guest user, Show Other People's Bookings As set to Busy for site guests so visitors never see other people's names, and an activated site. Flow recipes are no-code (Parse Date Entries from JSON, Roll-Up Summary or a Record-Triggered Flow). Includes a searchable reference of 100+ properties by label and API name.

## Accessibility & VPAT 2.5 | MultiDatePick (https://multidatepick.com/accessibility.html)

VPAT 2.5 self-attested conformance report against WCAG 2.1 A/AA, Revised Section 508, and EN 301 549 V3.2.1.

- Product version: managed package 0.13.0-16, and the features coming in 0.14.0 (Map view and location picker, custom action buttons, series editing, the Unscheduled list, header branding, record details pop-up). Report date: November 10, 2026. Last verified: November 10, 2026 on the unpackaged source; November 7, 2026 on the managed package install.
- Scope: the Dates, Dates & Times and Resource Booking components, the six views (Calendar, Timeline, Week, Utilization, Agenda and Map), the location picker and the Setup Wizard. In the Map view and the location picker, the list, labels, buttons and keyboard handling are MultiDatePick's; the map tiles and pins come from Salesforce's map service (lightning-map) in its own frame and are covered by Salesforce's VPAT, as is Salesforce's page chrome.
- Method: axe-core 4.11 (WCAG 2.1 A and AA rules) scoped to the MultiDatePick component; text contrast measured from computed styles; keyboard tests of the new features (Tab order, Enter, Space, Escape, focus into each pop-up and back, visible focus, 390 pixels wide and 200% zoom); code review of ARIA roles, names and keyboard handling.
- Scan results: zero violations on all nine surfaces and the new features. Rules passed: Dates 17, Dates & Times 17, Resource Booking 17, Calendar view 18, Timeline 17, Week 16, Utilization 17, Agenda 16, Map view 20; location picker 17, custom action buttons and Screen Flow pop-up 14, series editing 17, Unscheduled list 14, record details pop-up 15.
- Two checks flagged for manual review everywhere: ARIA id references inside Lightning's shadow DOM (ids confirmed in code), and contrast, which axe could not compute inside the component, so it was measured from computed styles: with the default colors every text element meets its minimum (0.14.0 darkened some secondary text that is about 3:1 in 0.13.0-16).
- Calendar uses ARIA grid markup with aria-selected; the view switcher is a labeled button group with aria-pressed; every booking bar, week block, heatmap cell, agenda row and Map list item is a native button with an accessible name; in the Map view, Enter on a list item opens the record's card and Tab reaches its link and action buttons; pop-ups take focus and give it back when they close.
- Partially Supports: 1.4.3 Contrast (admins choose status colors) and 1.4.10 Reflow (Timeline, Week and Utilization scroll horizontally in narrow containers).
- 9 languages honoring the user's Salesforce Locale.
- Related: Section 508 guide for government teams at /blog/salesforce-section-508-government-calendar.html.

## Salesforce Add to Calendar: Bookings Into Outlook and Google (https://multidatepick.com/blog/salesforce-add-to-calendar.html)

Give every Salesforce booking an Add to Calendar button: one .ics file for Outlook, Google and Apple Calendar after Save, even for Experience Cloud guests. No code.

A booking saved in Salesforce is only half done until it is in the person's own calendar. Turn on Show Add to Calendar After Saving and every successful save offers an Add to Calendar button that downloads one .ics calendar file with an event for each record just saved: the record name as the title, the saved date and times (date-only records as all-day events, a range as one event), the resource as the location, the status as the description and the Salesforce record Id as the unique ID. It opens in Outlook, Google Calendar and Apple Calendar; when a browser cannot create the file, a single booking gets an Add to Google Calendar link. The file is built in the browser, so it works for guests on public Experience Cloud booking pages, and it needs no connected app, OAuth or outbound callout: MultiDatePick stays 100% native. It is a one-time file rather than a live sync, so a booking that moves later needs a fresh file. Setup is one checkbox on the component or the Setup Wizard config.

## The Salesforce Account Calendar: Every Related Record in One View (https://multidatepick.com/blog/salesforce-calendar-related-records.html)

Show tasks and records from contacts, opportunities and custom objects on one Salesforce account calendar. One Rollup Field, up to five lookups deep, no Apex.

- Published October 31, 2026.
- The problem: a calendar on a record page normally loads only the records that look up to that record (one level). On an Account page with a Task calendar that is the tasks whose Related To is the account; tasks logged on the account's contacts and opportunities are left out, and so are grandchild records of custom objects.
- Rollup Field (component property rollupField; Setup Wizard Fields screen, "Also" box): a second field, or a path through lookups, that also leads back to the page record. The calendar shows every record that matches the Relationship Field API Name OR the Rollup Field.
- New records still save through the Relationship Field API Name. Rollup Field only widens what the calendar shows.
- Paths use Salesforce relationship notation, up to five levels: AccountId, Project__r.Account__c, Location__r.Region__r.Account__c, Quote__r.OpportunityId.
- Example from the post (Northwind Logistics demo account): a Task calendar saved through WhatId showed 4 marked days in November with the account's own tasks; with Rollup Field AccountId it showed 11, adding the contact's calls and the opportunity's milestones.
- Records load as the viewing user, so record sharing and field-level security apply.
- Components: Dates and Dates & Times, for any standard or custom object. The Resource Booking component uses Rollup Field with This Record Only, so its Timeline, Week, Utilization and Agenda views show the bookings tied to the page record through the lookup path.
- Setup: Setup Wizard > Account record page > one record per date > Fields: Task, Relationship Field API Name Related To ID (WhatId), Date Field API Name ActivityDate, Rollup Field AccountId > save a Config Name > add the Dates component to the Account page with that Config Name.
- Use cases: account managers, field service (site visits per location), project delivery, customer success, nonprofits (household members), property management (unit inspections rolled up through the building).

## Create Salesforce Tasks From a Calendar: Pick the Days, Save Once (https://multidatepick.com/blog/create-salesforce-tasks-calendar.html)

Create multiple Salesforce Tasks at once: pick the days on a calendar, set the subject, status and priority, and save one Task per day. No Flow, no Apex.

- Published November 8, 2026.
- The problem: the New Task button saves one task with one due date, and a recurring series repeats on a fixed schedule, so a plan of tasks on several chosen days is one trip through the form per task.
- What MultiDatePick does: the Dates component on a record page saves each picked day as its own standard Salesforce Task (Child Object API Name Task, Date Field API Name ActivityDate, Record Name Field Subject), linked to the page record, in one save.
- Linking: Related To (WhatId) on Accounts, Opportunities, Cases and custom objects with activities; Name (WhoId) on Contacts and Leads. On a Contact page Salesforce also fills the task's account, so the tasks show on the account too. Verified in a Salesforce org on 2026-11-08 for Contact and Lead pages.
- Filled on every new task: the subject typed in the Record Label box, the status from the status picker, and any other field through Default Field Values, for example Priority=High, a Comments line (Description), or OwnerId set to a user's Id to assign the tasks. Without OwnerId, tasks are assigned to the person who saves them.
- The tasks are ordinary Salesforce Tasks: they show in the record's Activity timeline, on the Tasks tab, in reports and list views. The post's example: four Customer check-in tasks on the Northwind Logistics account, each flagged High priority.
- Picking: click scattered days, drag across a run, or Add Recurring Pattern (every Tuesday, every other week, 1st to 4th or last weekday of the month, up to an end date). Each day still saves as its own Task. Allow Multiple Per Day lets a day with a task take another.
- Seeing tasks: on a record page the calendar shows that record's tasks in status colors with hover details. On an app or Home page, Show All Records with Record Filter OwnerId=ME gives each person a calendar of their own tasks; Show Record Names in Each Day writes each subject in its day; status pills filter by status. Edit Mode moves, re-statuses or deletes tasks, one or many at once.
- Setup: Setup Wizard > record page (for example Account) > one record per date > Fields: click Task, Relationship Field Related To ID (WhatId) or Name ID (WhoId), Due Date Only (ActivityDate), Subject; default subject, untick Append Date/Time to Record Name, Default Field Values such as Priority=High > save a Config Name > add the MultiDatePick Dates component in Lightning App Builder with that Config Name.
- Use cases: account managers (quarterly check-ins), sales follow-up (day 2, 7 and 14 after a demo), customer success onboarding, compliance and finance deadlines, nonprofit donor stewardship, service follow-ups after a case closes.
- Record details pop-up (Setup Wizard, Fields screen; component property recordForm): Save (or Book) first opens a form with the fields the admin chooses, with required marks, default values and half or full width. Fill in: the same for every picked day, each day its own, or let the user choose. On a Dates calendar it can instead open when a day is clicked, one record at a time. Only fields the user can create are offered. Works for Experience Cloud guests too (lookup fields are left out for guests).

## Best Salesforce Calendar Apps and LWC Calendars (2026) (https://multidatepick.com/blog/best-salesforce-calendar-apps.html)

A comparison of eight ways to put a calendar in Salesforce, written by MultiDatePick; statements about other products come from their public pages as of November 2026.

- Options: MultiDatePick (no-code calendar LWC suite: multi-date picking, time slots, resource booking with capacity, seven views, Screen Flows, guest booking), the built-in Salesforce Calendar (Events and object date fields on Day, Week, Month and Table views), Salesforce Scheduler, formerly Lightning Scheduler (appointments on its own data model, add-on license), CalendarAnything (calendar views over any object: Gantt, swimlane, Kanban, mail-calendar integrations), DayBack (drag-and-drop calendar over Salesforce objects and external calendars), Avonni Components (a component library configured in Flow Builder or App Builder), GoMeddo, formerly Booker25 (booking platform with a website widget and SDK), FullCalendar in an LWC (open-source library your developers wrap and maintain).
- Comparison rows, in buyer order: native on your own objects, setup without code, picking many dates and saving them as records, booking rules built in, views, a Screen Flow component with outputs, guest booking on Experience Cloud. Project plans with task dependencies is a row too (only MultiDatePick links tasks in a Gantt view). MultiDatePick wins 6 rows and ties 2; no other option wins a row.
- How to choose: rooms, equipment or people with seat limits (/salesforce-booking-calendar.html), customers booking on a website (/salesforce-calendar-experience-cloud-booking.html), weighing Salesforce's own product (/salesforce-calendar-vs-lightning-scheduler.html), many dates (/multidatepickdates.html), time slots (/multidatepickdatetime.html), classes with seats (/salesforce-class-scheduling.html), a code-first option (/blog/fullcalendar-salesforce-lwc-vs-multidatepick.html).
- FAQ: the best calendar app for Salesforce, a customizable LWC calendar, whether Salesforce has a built-in booking calendar, FullCalendar in Salesforce, Experience Cloud guest booking without login.

## Salesforce Appointment Scheduling: Set Times for Every Advisor, No Code (https://multidatepick.com/blog/salesforce-appointment-scheduling.html)

Salesforce appointment scheduling with no code: offer only the times you choose, set times per advisor, keep clients private, and let them book on your site.

- Published November 12, 2026.
- Who it is for: financial advisors, clinics and therapists, salons and spas, consultants, service teams and university advising. Appointments are booked by staff on a record page, an app page or a Screen Flow, or by clients on a public Experience Cloud page without logging in. Every appointment saves as a record on the customer's own object (custom or standard). No Apex, no add-on license.
- Only These Times (on the Date and Time and Resource Booking components): the only start times people can pick, in 24-hour form separated by commas, for example 09:00,10:30,13:00,14:30,16:00. Each lasts the Booking Length, or the Time Interval when Booking Length is blank. While set, Time Interval and Earliest/Latest Time are not used. In the Setup Wizard: Start times, then Only these times, then Add a time.
- Each advisor's own times (Only These Times Field, on Resource Booking): the API name of a text field on the resource object holding that resource's own start times in the same form (for example Available_Times__c holding 08:00,09:30,11:00). A picked advisor uses their own times; a blank value falls back to Only These Times, or every interval. Several resources booked together offer only the times all of them list.
- A listed time that is booked, closed, too soon for the notice period, outside the advisor's business hours, or too close to the next booking for the buffer shows greyed out rather than disappearing.
- Per advisor: Business Hours Start Field and Business Hours End Field (time fields on the resource); closures (days off, office closures, partial days) from a closures object with an optional resource field and a reason label.
- Booking Length (Minutes): one click books the whole appointment. Buffer Between Bookings (Minutes) keeps time free after each one.
- Privacy: Show Other People's Bookings As = Details, Busy for site guests, or Busy. Busy draws other people's appointments as a hatched Unavailable block with no name, no hover card and no link; names and fields are removed on the server.
- Rules, checked again on the server at every save: Minimum Notice (Hours), Book Up To (Days Ahead), Limit per Person with a Client Field (email, text, or a lookup to Contact, Lead, Account or User; staff can book past it after a confirmation, site visitors cannot), Max Bookings per Day, closed days, buffers, conflict checks.
- Client details: the Record Details Pop-up asks a site guest for name, email, meeting type and a note before the appointment saves.
- Statuses: Status Field with a color per status (for example Requested, Confirmed, Met, No-Show, Cancelled); Selectable Statuses sets what a new booking saves as (Requested on a public page); Ignored Statuses (for example Cancelled) frees the time. Confirmation message: Show In-Component Toast plus Success Toast Message.
- Custom buttons (Setup Wizard): a Send a reminder button on each appointment runs the admin's own Flow; buttons can be limited to statuses, act on appointments picked in Edit Mode, or run on their own after every save (for example a confirmation email Flow).
- Add to Calendar: Show Add to Calendar After Saving gives the client a calendar file (.ics) for Outlook, Google and Apple Calendar, built in the browser, so site guests get it too.
- Compared with Salesforce Scheduler: Scheduler is an add-on license on its own data model; MultiDatePick books on the objects you already have for $20 per user per month with every feature.
- FAQ: scheduling appointments in Salesforce without code, offering only set times, each advisor's own times, guest booking on Experience Cloud, whether clients see other clients, whether Salesforce Scheduler is needed.

## Brand Your Salesforce Calendar: Your Logo, Colors and a Banner Photo (https://multidatepick.com/blog/brand-your-salesforce-calendar.html)

Brand your Salesforce calendar with no code: your logo, name and brand colors on its top band, plus a banner photo, set in the Setup Wizard. Guests see it too.

- Published November 9, 2026.
- The problem: a calendar component arrives in its maker's colors, and changing them usually takes a stylesheet, a static resource or a developer. Admins ask how to add a logo to a Salesforce calendar and how to make an Experience Cloud booking page match their brand.
- Where it is set: MultiDatePick Setup Wizard > Other settings > Header box, with a live preview at the top of the box. No code, no CSS, no static resource. Nothing changes until an admin sets it; a calendar with no Header keeps its standard band.
- Logo: upload one, pick one of your own images in Salesforce Files, or paste an image link. Shown up to 44 px high and 180 px wide (64 px high on the Cover strip), left of the title or above it, centered, on a white tile by default (White tile behind the logo can be turned off for a logo made for dark backgrounds).
- Words: Name above the calendar's title (up to 80 characters), Line under the title and Note (up to 160 characters each). The calendar keeps its own title.
- Colors: Band color (six swatches or any hex code) and Button color (five swatches or any hex code). The button color paints the Today button, the outline on today's date, and the picked days and time slots. A dark or mid-tone band color also colors the calendar's own buttons (Save, Request Appointment) and the selected view; a light band keeps the standard navy there.
- Readability: Words on the band is Automatic, Light or Dark. Automatic writes dark or light words, whichever reads better on the band color. Where the color sits under white words (buttons, the selected view) it is deepened just enough to pass 4.5:1 contrast, the WCAG AA level for text. The wizard flags a Light or Dark choice that is hard to read on the band color, and one that cannot be read falls back to Automatic. With a photo behind the band (every look but Cover strip) the words stay light over the shade, or dark on a light tinted band.
- Banner image, in four looks: Behind the band, Cover strip (a photo strip across the top, the band color under it, the logo on its edge), Controls on a panel (the photo in full, the name and controls on dark panels), Tinted in band color. Shade 0 to 90 percent (the wizard warns when a light shade could make words hard to read on a bright photo; on the tinted look it sets how strongly the band color covers the photo), Keep in view (center, top, bottom, left or right: the part of the photo kept on screen when the calendar is narrow), Height (Compact, Standard, Tall). JPG or PNG at least 1600 px wide works best.
- Public pages: an image uploaded in the wizard or picked from the admin's own Salesforce Files gets a standard Salesforce public link (Content Deliveries and Public Links on in Setup), so Experience Cloud guests who never log in see the logo and photo. An image link from another website shows once that site is added in Setup under Trusted URLs; if a link fails to load, the calendar shows the band without the picture and the wizard says so under the link.
- App Builder, Experience Builder and Flow Builder: one property, Header (headerStyle), JSON with the keys logo, logoPos (left or above), logoTile (true or false), name, sub, note, band, button, text (auto, light, dark), image, look (behind, cover, panel, tint), shade (0 to 0.9), focus (center, top, bottom, left, right), height (compact, standard, tall). On all three components (Dates, Dates & Times, Resource Booking), on record, app and Home pages, Experience Cloud pages and Flow screens. A Setup Wizard config carries it through Config Name.
- The band sits above every view (Calendar, Timeline, Week, Utilization, Agenda, Map, Gantt).
- Use cases: financial advisors (client booking pages in firm colors), clinics and practices (name and opening hours), universities (school colors, campus photo), multi-location brands (one config per location), nonprofits (volunteer sign-ups), company apps (a Home page calendar in company colors).

## Salesforce Campaign Calendar: Every Event Date, No Apex (https://multidatepick.com/blog/salesforce-campaign-multiple-dates.html)

Track every date of a Salesforce Campaign on one calendar: tour stops, webinar series and volunteer days saved as child records, with status colors. No Apex.

A Campaign has one start date and one end date. Your tour, webinar series or volunteer program has many. Put them all on the Campaign record, each one a real record with a status, without writing Apex.
"How do I add more than one date to a Salesforce Campaign?" "Where do I track each stop of the roadshow?" "Which webinar sessions are confirmed?" A Campaign only knows when it starts and ends. Everything in between ends up in a spreadsheet or a long description field.
MultiDatePick puts a calendar on the Campaign record page. Click the days, save, and each one becomes its own child record linked to the Campaign, colored by status. It works on Campaigns the same way it works on any object: by configuration. No Apex required.

### What you get on the Campaign page
- **Every date at a glance**
All of the Campaign's dates load onto the calendar when the record opens. No related list to scroll.
- **Status colors**
Planned, Confirmed, Completed, Cancelled: each status gets its own color, and the pills above the calendar filter by status.
- **Hover for details**
Point at a date to see the record behind it, such as the stop name, venue and status, with a link to open it.
- **Recurring patterns**
Every Tuesday for eight weeks is one pattern and one click. Handy for webinar series and send schedules.
- **Edit mode**
Select several dates, then change their status, move them to another day, or delete them in one step.
- **Real records**
Each date is a child record with a lookup to the Campaign. Report on it, build flows on it, share it like anything else.

### Set it up in three steps
The components are object-agnostic. They do not know or care that the parent is a Campaign; they need a child object to save into and a lookup that points back. That is the whole integration.
- Create the child object. In Object Manager, create a custom object such as Campaign Date. Give it a Lookup field to Campaign and a Date field. Add a Status picklist (Planned, Confirmed, Completed, Cancelled) and any detail fields you want on hover, such as Venue.
- Run the Setup Wizard. Open the MultiDatePick Setup Wizard tab and configure the Dates component. Pick Campaign Date as the object, the Campaign lookup as the relationship field and your Date field. On Status & Display, choose the status field, a color per value and the hover fields. Save the config under a name like Campaign_Dates.
- Drop the component on the Campaign page. Open any Campaign, click Edit Page, drag the MultiDatePick Dates component onto the layout and enter the config name in Config Name. Save and activate. Every Campaign now has its calendar.
Need times as well as days, like a webinar at 11:00 and a repeat at 3:00? Use the Dates & Times component instead and add Start and End Time fields to the child object. The steps are the same.

### Prefer a Screen Flow?
The same config works inside Flow. Add the Dates component to a screen and set Config Name; every setting comes from the config, with no checkboxes to set in Flow Builder. Pass the Campaign Id into Parent Record Id and the component saves the child records itself. Leave it blank if you would rather loop the Selected Dates output and create the records your own way. The multiple dates in a Screen Flow post walks through both patterns.

### What teams track on Campaigns
Anything a Campaign does on more than one day fits the same child object:

### The settings that shape it
Each one is a field in the Setup Wizard and a property on the component, so nothing here needs code:

### Questions people ask
Q: Can a Salesforce Campaign have multiple dates?
A standard Campaign has one Start Date and one End Date. To track every day of a tour, webinar series or volunteer program, add a small child object with a lookup to Campaign and put the MultiDatePick Dates component on the Campaign record page. Every date you click is saved as its own child record.
Q: Do I need Apex or a developer to add dates to Campaigns?
No. The child object and its fields are point-and-click in Object Manager, the Setup Wizard writes the calendar configuration, and the component goes on the page in Lightning App Builder. There is no Campaign-specific code to write or install.
Q: Where are the Campaign dates stored?
In your own custom object, for example Campaign Date, with one record per date and a lookup to the Campaign. They are ordinary Salesforce records, so list views, reports, flows and sharing all work on them as usual.
Q: Can each Campaign date have its own status?
Yes. Add a picklist such as Planned, Confirmed, Completed and Cancelled, choose a color for each value, and the calendar paints every date in its status color. Edit mode lets you select several dates and change their status, move them, or delete them in one step.
Q: Can I use it in a Screen Flow instead of the record page?
Yes. Add the Dates component to a flow screen and set Config Name to the config you saved in the Setup Wizard. Pass the Campaign Id into Parent Record Id and the component saves the child records itself, or leave it blank and loop the Selected Dates output.

## Salesforce Utilization Heatmap: See Who Is Overbooked (https://multidatepick.com/blog/salesforce-utilization-heatmap.html)

A Salesforce utilization heatmap: each resource down the side, every day showing booked against capacity, overbooking flagged, one click into the schedule.

Every room, person or asset down the side, every day across the top, and each cell showing how much of its capacity is booked. A capacity dashboard for your own Salesforce objects, set up without code.
"Is the team overbooked next week?" "Which room sits empty most of the month?" "Can we take on one more engagement?" Those are capacity questions. A calendar shows what is booked; it does not show how full anything is. A utilization heatmap does.
MultiDatePick's Utilization view reads the same bookings as its calendar and timeline and turns them into a grid of fill levels: one row per resource, one cell per day, each cell saying how many of that resource's places are taken. It is one config field away from any placement, and it needs nothing more than a number on the resource for capacity.

### What the heatmap shows
- **Booked of capacity**
Each cell reads like 3/4: three of four places taken. The fuller the day, the darker the blue.
- **Overbooking flagged**
A day booked past capacity gets an orange ring. It is never quietly capped at "full".
- **Combined availability**
A row across the top shows the whole group's fill per day as a percentage, so the crunch days stand out.
- **Average and open**
The right-hand column gives each resource's average for the month and how many places are still open from today.
- **Click to drill in**
Click a booked cell and the component opens that resource's week on that day, ready to book or edit.
- **Works without capacity**
No capacity field yet? Cells show a plain count of bookings on the same scale, and the grid says so.

### A month of capacity in one look
Reports can tell you utilization, one question at a time. The heatmap shows the whole month at once, so patterns jump out that a report would never surface: the advisor who is full every Tuesday, the room nobody books on Fridays, the week where everyone is at capacity at the same time. The grid opens on today, keeps resource names pinned while you scroll, and counts open places only from today forward, because unused capacity last week cannot be booked anymore.

### Multi-day work counts on every day it runs
Capacity covers more than meetings. A consultant can carry two client engagements at a time; a crew can work one job site at once; a training room hosts one course for a whole week. The heatmap counts a multi-day booking on every day it covers, so an engagement that runs Monday to Friday fills all five cells. Set the capacity to the number of things a resource can carry at once and the grid shows exactly when each person is fully committed.

### Who uses a Salesforce utilization heatmap
The resource can be any object, so the same view answers capacity questions for very different teams:

### The settings that shape it
Every one of these is a property on the component and a field in the Setup Wizard, so nothing here needs code:

### Questions people ask
Q: How do I see resource utilization in Salesforce?
Standard Salesforce has no utilization view for your own booking objects; you would build a report per question. MultiDatePick adds a Utilization view to the calendar component: each resource is a row, each day a cell showing booked against that resource's capacity, with a combined row for the whole group and an average and open count on the right.
Q: What does a cell like 2/2 or 3/4 mean?
Bookings on that day against the resource's capacity. 3/4 means three of four places are taken. The darker the blue, the fuller the day, and a day booked past capacity gets an orange ring so it stands out.
Q: What if my resource object has no capacity field?
The heatmap still works. Cells show a plain count of bookings on the same blue scale, and a note under the grid says so. Add a number field for capacity whenever you want percentages and open places instead.
Q: Can I book or edit from the Utilization view?
Utilization is read only by design: it answers how full things are. Click any booked cell and the component opens that resource's week on that day, where you can book, move or edit.
Q: Can the rows be people instead of rooms?
Yes. The resource can be any object, including User. Add a capacity number to User and the heatmap becomes a team capacity dashboard: who is full, who has room, and which weeks are overloaded.

## Salesforce Timeline View: Every Resource on One Screen (https://multidatepick.com/blog/salesforce-timeline-view.html)

A Salesforce resource timeline: rooms, people and equipment down the side, dates across, multi-day bookings as one bar, and drag to reschedule. No code.

Rooms, people, equipment or projects down the side, dates across the top, and every booking drawn as one bar. A resource timeline for any Salesforce object, set up without code.
"Which room is free next Tuesday?" "Who on the team has capacity this week?" "When does the van come back?" Each of those is a question about many resources across many days, and a month calendar answers it one resource at a time. A timeline answers it in one look.
MultiDatePick's Timeline view puts every resource on its own row and every booking on a bar that runs exactly as long as the booking does. It reads your own Salesforce objects, saves through the same path as the rest of the component, and is one config field away from any placement.

### What the timeline does that a calendar cannot
- **One bar per booking**
A booking that runs Monday to Friday is one continuous bar, so its length is visible at a glance.
- **Lanes for overlaps**
Overlapping bookings on a resource stack into lanes. A busy day collapses to a count you expand in place.
- **Capacity strip**
A strip above each group shows how full every day is against the resources' combined capacity.
- **Day, Week and Month zoom**
Hours across for today, two weeks for planning, a month for the long view. One click between them.
- **Drag to reschedule**
Slide a bar to move it, pull an edge to stretch it. It saves on release and stays where you put it.
- **Book from the grid**
Drag across empty days on a resource's row to select them, then book. The row picks the resource for you.

### Drag to reschedule, stretch to extend
Plans change, and changing one should not mean opening a record, editing two date fields and saving. On the timeline you grab the bar. Pull its right edge and the booking runs longer; grab the middle and it slides to other days. The bar shows the dates it will land on while you drag, saves the moment you let go, and stays in its lane with a brief highlight so you can see exactly what changed.
Switch to Day zoom and the columns become hours. The same gestures then move and stretch a booking's start and end times, so a meeting that runs over is one drag to fix.

### Capacity you can see at a glance
Above the rows, a capacity strip shades every day by how much of the resources' combined capacity is booked, so the crunch weeks stand out before anyone asks. Group rows by a picklist or lookup (building, team, region) and each group gets its own strip. When one resource has several bookings on the same day, they stack into lanes; a day with more than a few collapses to a count that expands in place when you click it.

The resource can be any object, so the same view fits very different teams:

### The settings that shape it
Every one of these is a property on the component and a field in the Setup Wizard, so nothing here needs code:

### Questions people ask
Q: Does Salesforce have a timeline view for resources?
Not as a standard Lightning component for your own objects. Calendars in Salesforce show one person's events. MultiDatePick adds a resource timeline that reads any custom or standard object: pick the object that holds bookings and the object that holds resources, and every resource becomes a row.
Q: Can I drag bookings on the timeline to reschedule them?
Yes. With Edit Mode on, grab the middle of a bar to move it to other days or either edge to change its start or end. The bar shows its new dates while you drag and saves when you let go. In Day zoom the same gestures move and stretch the booking's start and end times.
Q: Can the rows be people instead of rooms?
Yes. The resource can be any object, including User. Point it at User and the timeline becomes a staff roster: each person a row, their shifts, visits or assignments as bars.
Q: How do I stop a long list of resources turning into a wall of rows?
Set Max View Resources to draw only the busiest rows, group rows under a picklist or lookup with Timeline Group By Field, and choose whether rows show all resources or only ones with bookings. Every resource still counts toward capacity; the settings only change what is drawn.
Q: Does the timeline work on Experience Cloud sites and record pages?
Yes. It is one of seven views in the same component, so it runs anywhere the component does: record pages, app and home pages, Flow screens and Experience Cloud sites.

## Section 508 Calendar for Salesforce Government Orgs (https://multidatepick.com/blog/salesforce-section-508-government-calendar.html)

State and local agencies now have until April 2027 to meet WCAG 2.1 AA. What that means for scheduling in Salesforce, and the accessible calendar built for it.

Agencies on Salesforce book inspections, appointments, facilities and field staff every day. The federal deadline for making those pages accessible just moved to April 2027. Here is what it asks of the calendar, and how MultiDatePick answers it.
In April 2024 the Department of Justice set a firm technical standard for state and local government websites and apps under ADA Title II: WCAG 2.1 Level AA. In April 2026 it gave agencies one more year to get there. That year is the window to fix the parts of your Salesforce org that residents and staff actually click, and the scheduling calendar is near the top of that list.

### The dates that apply now
An interim final rule published April 20, 2026 extended both compliance dates by one year. The standard itself did not change.
Two things are easy to miss. First, many articles still quote April 2026, which is out of date. Second, the Justice Department is explicit that the obligation to make services accessible did not pause: the dates set when the specific technical standard becomes enforceable, not when accessibility starts to matter. Federal agencies were never on this clock at all; they answer to Section 508, which already requires WCAG 2.0 AA, and every one of those criteria is also part of 2.1 AA.

### Where scheduling shows up in a government org
Almost every public service on Salesforce has a calendar in it.
- **Inspections**
Homeowners pick a day for a building or permit inspection.
- **Appointments**
Residents book licensing, benefits and records visits.
- **Facility rentals**
Families reserve pavilions, ballfields and community rooms.
- **Clinics**
Vaccination slots with a fixed number of seats per hour.
- **Field staff**
Inspectors, caseworkers and poll workers scheduled across a month.
- **Closures**
Meeting rooms blocked for holidays and maintenance.

### What MultiDatePick does, criterion by criterion
MultiDatePick was built with WCAG 2.1 AA as its target from the start. This is what that looks like in the component your residents and staff actually use:
The VPAT marks two criteria as Partially Supports, and says exactly why. Contrast: the default palette meets 4.5:1, but admins can choose their own status colors, and a vendor cannot guarantee a color it did not pick. Reflow: at 320 pixels wide the month grid keeps its seven columns and narrows rather than stacking. Procurement reviewers trust a report that explains its partials over a wall of unexplained Supports.

### How it compares
Agencies usually weigh four ways to put a scheduling calendar in Salesforce. Only one of them gives you multi-date and resource booking, published accessibility documentation and resident data that never leaves your org, all on day one.
The standard date field is accessible, but it holds one date, so it cannot run a booking. An external tool can book, but residents' names, addresses and appointment history then live in someone else's system, which is a second security review and a second accessibility review. A custom build keeps the data home, but your team now owns the WCAG testing, the VPAT and every fix, forever. MultiDatePick is the only option on the list that clears every row.

### Built for how government buys
- 100% Salesforce native. No external servers, no outbound callouts, no subprocessors. Resident data stays in your org under the sharing and field-level security you already configured, so there is no new data processor to approve. See Trust & Security.
- Passed Salesforce's AppExchange security review. The managed package went through Salesforce's own review before listing.
- Resident self-service. The Resource Booking component runs on Experience Cloud sites, so residents can pick an inspection window or reserve a facility on the same accessible calendar staff use.
- No code to maintain. A Setup Wizard writes the configuration, with a live preview of the real component, so a small IT team is not signing up for a custom build it has to keep compliant.

### Getting ready before April 2027
- Inventory every date picker your public touches. Experience Cloud pages first, then staff Screen Flows. Note which ones are standard fields and which are third-party or custom components.
- Request a current VPAT for every third-party component. Check the report date and that it was tested on the packaged version you actually install.
- Test the booking path with a keyboard alone. Pick a date, choose a time, save. If you cannot finish without a mouse, neither can a resident who relies on a keyboard or a screen reader.

## Salesforce Calendar: What It Does and What It Leaves Out (https://multidatepick.com/salesforce-calendar.html)

The built-in Salesforce Calendar (Lightning Experience) shows Events, plus coworker, public and resource calendars, in Day, Week and Month views, with a Table view that lists events. Users can build calendars from any object with a date or date/time field, filtered by a list view, and create recurring events as an event series. Day, week and month views show up to 150 or 500 items in total, depending on setup (Salesforce Help).

Where it stops: each record shows on one date or one start to end span; clicking a slot creates one Event, so there is no way to select a set of days and save them to a record; resource calendars show bookings but do not count capacity; the calendar lives on its own Calendar page; there is no resource timeline or capacity heatmap.

MultiDatePick picks up from there: click or drag any number of days on one calendar, recurring patterns (weekdays, weekends, custom days, every N weeks), a time slot for each date at any interval, resource booking with booked of capacity badges and a conflict check on save, and seven views (Calendar, Timeline, Week, Utilization, Agenda, Map, Gantt). It runs on record, App and Home pages, Screen Flows and Experience Cloud sites, and writes your own child records. Keep the Salesforce Calendar for your own meetings and email sync; use MultiDatePick wherever a record needs many dates, times or bookings. $20/user/month, every feature, 30-day free trial.

One Salesforce calendar suite for the four scheduling jobs of a staffing agency, saved to your own objects with no code.

- Shifts and placements (Resource Booking component): a Capacity Field on the job or shift keeps a slot open until it is full, with live booked of capacity badges. Business hours per role.

Interview scheduling inside Salesforce with MultiDatePick: offer real slots, catch clashes before they happen, and save every round as a record on your own object.

## Salesforce Class Scheduling: Course Sessions With Seat Limits (https://multidatepick.com/salesforce-class-scheduling.html)

Class and course scheduling in Salesforce with the MultiDatePick Resource Booking component, set up with no code.

- Each class session is a time slot on a training room or course record with a seat limit (a number field chosen as Capacity Field). Every slot shows a live badge such as 9/12; the last seat closes the slot; a cancelled enrollment frees its seat (Cancelled in Ignored Statuses).

- One session in several rooms at once: several resources with Capacity Aggregation set to Distinct count as one booking (Multi-Site Workshop config).
- Views for coordinators: Timeline (rooms or trainers against dates), Utilization (how full each room is), Calendar and Agenda.
- Starter configs in the Config Library: Training Batch Enrollment and Multi-Site Workshop.

Meeting room and desk booking inside Salesforce with the MultiDatePick Resource Booking component. Rooms are records on any object. People pick a room, pick one or many days, click open time slots and book; each booking saves as a record on your own booking object.
